title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: under mixed-priority traffic the continuous batcher scheduler showed starvation of low-priority requests and occasional head-of-line latency spikes during sustained bursts. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, introduce starvation prevention, and make request timeouts explicit and configurable.

Summary of changes: implement age-based request aging to boost priority over time, add per-queue max_wait_ms and a global soft-timeout soft_dispatch_deadline to prevent indefinite waiting, add explicit timeouts and metrics for queue wait and starvation, and introduce heuristic time-based flushing for long-tailed requests. Also added unit and integration tests, small docs, and a canary rollout plan.

Checklist: 
- [x] Age-based priority adjustment for fairness
- [x] Per-queue and global timeout knobs
- [x] Metrics for queue_wait_seconds, scheduler_starvation_count, dispatched_after_timeout
- [x] Unit tests for fairness and timeout behavior
- [x] Integration perf runs and canary rollout configuration
- [x] Docs for new config flags and recommended defaults

Notes: Default behavior is backward-compatible: if the new config block is omitted we preserve current scheduling semantics. We chose conservative defaults after perf lab runs: default max_wait_ms=5000ms for LOW priority, 2500ms for MED, 800ms for HIGH; global soft_dispatch_deadline=1200ms to avoid pathological waits under heavy load. These values are tunable via the continuous_batcher.scheduler config.

Linear references: ENG-2124 implements the scheduler work, ENG-2140 tracks canary rollout and dashboards. Related: perf canary runs in perf-canary repo and follow-up tuning may change defaults depending on customer workloads.
commits: 5 commits: 1) scheduler: add age-based priority uplift and max_wait enforcement; 2) scheduler: soft_dispatch_deadline and heuristic flush; 3) metrics: queue_wait_seconds histogram + starvation counter; 4) tests: unit + integration fairness/timeouts; 5) docs and canary config
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Looks good overall; please add a comment explaining the aging formula and why we chose linear uplift vs exponential (requested).

Author (Asha): Replaced the map update with a fine-grained lock in lock_utils.py and added unit test that previously reproduced the race. Re-ran CI — integration now passes.

perf_impact_summary: Benchmarks (perf-lab synthetic mixed-priority workload, 50k reqs over 5m) show: p50 latency unchanged, p90 latency reduced by ~18% under 90th-percentile load due to earlier flushes, p99 latency reduced by ~22% from fewer head-of-line stalls. Throughput improved by ~6% at target latency SLOs because starvation reduction allowed better packing of batches. CPU overhead of scheduler increased ~2% due to additional bookkeeping.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for age-based uplift and timeout enforcement. Integration test reproduces mixed-priority burst scenario and validates no starvation for low-priority requests over long runs. Perf-canary run executed against a small subset of traffic for 24h; dashboards show expected metrics and no regressions. Post-merge plan: 48h canary at 5% traffic, alert on dispatched_after_timeout > 0.5% of requests or p99 latency regression >15%.
release_notes:
- Improved continuous batcher scheduler to reduce starvation and head-of-line latency under mixed-priority workloads.
- New config knobs: continuous_batcher.scheduler.max_wait_ms (per-priority) and continuous_batcher.scheduler.soft_dispatch_deadline (global).
- Added metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_wait_seconds, continuous_batcher.scheduler_starvation_count, continuous_batcher.dispatched_after_timeout.
- Default behavior preserves previous semantics when config is omitted.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: changing scheduling heuristics may alter tail-latency for some workloads. Mitigation: conservative default values, comprehensive unit/integration tests, canary rollout with specific alerting on dispatched_after_timeout and p99 latency, and easy rollback by reverting config. Added feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler.enable_aging (off by default during initial canary).
notes: Hotfix follow-up: a separate small hotfix PR will backfill a missing JSON encoding field for metric tags discovered during canary; tracked in ENG-2151.
